subject: Customer-owned storage & erase SLA for private nodes
messages:
From: Laura Sato <laura.sato@meridianhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@procurement.meridian.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions about customer-controlled storage & erase confirmation for our Private deployment

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move to contract review we need to align on two things for our Private/VPC deployment:

1) Data residency assurances — we require an explicit statement that all customer data (models, KV cache, logs, uploads) remains in the customer-managed object store in our AWS account and does not get replicated to Redwood-hosted buckets.

2) Deletion / erase SLA — we need to know the exact timeline and steps Redwood will take to permanently remove customer data on request, including how you handle backups, snapshots, and cached KV entries. We also need the form of attestation we will receive (signed acknowledgement, audit log extract, or both).

Can you outline the playbook and the expected SLA? We have SOC 2 timelines to match.

Appreciate a concise checklist we can attach to our procurement packet.

—Laura
Product Security, Meridian Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Laura Sato <laura.sato@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@procurement.meridian.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions about customer-controlled storage & erase confirmation for our Private deployment

Laura —

Thanks — good questions. Short answer up front: for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments we offer customer-controlled storage in your cloud account and a multi-step erase playbook. Below is a concise checklist; attaching a longer playbook as a PDF in a follow-up.

Key points (summary):
- Storage location: all persistent artifacts (model weights, embeddings, KV caches, user uploads, and logs that you opt to keep) are written to buckets/filesystems in your cloud account when you choose the customer-managed storage option. Redwood never writes permanent copies to a Redwood-managed bucket in that configuration.
- Key management: when you enable BYOK (customer-managed KMS keys), the fastest way to cryptographically render stored data unrecoverable is key destruction. We document both crypto-erase and physical deletion flows.
- Erase SLA: standard target is acknowledgement within 72 hours of a validated erase request; full completion and attestation depends on snapshot/fan-out lifecycle and can take up to 14 days for archival/replication purges in some object store configurations.
- Attestation: we provide an erase confirmation plus a slice of audit logs (request id, objects removed, timestamps) signed by our operations team. For contractual commitments we can supply a templated attestation letter.

I’m looping in Marissa (CS/ops) for details on the snapshot lifecycle and Neha for legal/compliance language. Tom — if procurement needs the attestation templated for your approval flow, let us know.

—Jordan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Laura Sato <laura.sato@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions about customer-controlled storage & erase confirmation for our Private deployment

Laura / Jordan —

Detail from ops perspective — practical notes to include in your packet:

1) What we delete vs what you control
- Customer-managed buckets: Redwood's runtime mounts or writes directly to the customer bucket (object keys are namespaced). We do not maintain a secondary permanent copy in our account.
- Runtime caches: ephemeral KV cache resides on instance-local NVMe; on a node teardown we zero the NVMe and reclaim. For customers who enable persistent KV caching to object storage we treat those as customer-owned and they follow the object-store erase flow.

2) Snapshots & backups
- Our service does periodic snapshots for safe restart and scaling; snapshots are stored in your account when you select customer-managed storage. Snapshots have a configurable retention window (default 7 days).
- If you ask for a full erase, we run a three-stage purge: mark, delete, verify. Mark flags objects; delete runs bulk deletes and lifecycle rule adjustments; verify collects deletion confirmations and checks for replicas/versions.

3) Timelines and edge cases
- Ack: 72 hours after validated request (validation includes verifying authorized requestor and cross-checking the account id).
- Bulk deletion: typical completion 3–7 days; up to 14 days if the provider has immutable object versions or cross-region replication delay.
- Crypto-erase shortcut: if BYOK is active and you authorize KMS key destruction, we can provide a crypto-erase attestation within 24 hours. Note: destroying a key is irreversible and must be coordinated with your security team.

4) What we provide back
- Signed PDF attestation (template attached).
- Audit log extract for the delete job (object IDs, delete timestamps, node ids).
- Optional live session to review the deletion run.

I attached the short playbook (redwood_vpc_data_handling.pdf) which expands on the above and includes the CLI commands we run during the purge.

—Marissa
Customer Operations Lead — Redwood Inference

Appreciate the details. A couple procurement/legal clarifications:
- We need the attestation template to include a statement that snapshots stored in our account will be expunged and that Redwood will provide a log excerpt showing object keys removed.
- Please confirm whether Redwood will accept a PO that ties the erase SLA to a service credit if the timeline is missed (we're proposing a 2% monthly credit for 30 days delayed).

If you can get us a sample attestation and a short note on SLA remedies we can circulate internally.

—Tom

Tom / Laura —

Thanks — next steps and deliverables (actionable checklist):

1) Attached: redwood_vpc_data_handling.pdf (ops playbook) and erase-procedure-2026.docx (attestation template + sample wording).
2) Attestation language: Neha has reviewed the template; short excerpt below for procurement: 
   - "Redwood Inference confirms that, for customer-managed storage in the customer's cloud account, Redwood will initiate and complete the deletion of customer-designated objects and snapshots per the agreed erase request workflow. Redwood will provide a signed erase attestation and an audit-log extract identifying deleted object keys and timestamps within the stated SLA."
3) SLA remedies: we are open to contract language that ties service credits to missed acknowledgement/completion milestones; please send your draft language. We typically negotiate on a case-by-case basis with SLA caps.
4) Crypto-erase option: if Meridian decides to use BYOK and authorizes key destruction, provide a single authorized signer and we will coordinate a 24-hour crypto-erase attestation. We will log the KMS key destruction event and include the key ID in the attestation.

If this looks good I propose a short call to finalize the attestation wording and procurement language — I have availability Wednesday morning PT.

—Jordan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
